summary: Western wear with sustained collector + workwear resale: cowboy boots (Lucchese/Tony Lama/Olathe/Anderson Bean), premium western hats (Stetson/Resistol/Greeley Hat Works), snap-front western shirts (Rockmount/Scully/H Bar C), vintage signed belt buckles (Montana Silversmiths/Crumrine/Bohlin/Sunset Trails), bolo ties, and vintage spurs (Crockett/Buermann/North & Judd). Strict focus on items that ship in poly mailer or small box; saddles, full tack sets, and oversized rodeo gear excluded. Sweet spot: $80-300 used resale on premium boots / hats / vintage buckles, $200-1500+ apex on signed Bohlin pieces and named-maker spurs.
field_workflow: Boots: makers' mark on the leather pull straps + size stamping inside the shaft
Boots: photograph the sole + outsole stitching — Lucchese has signature 'L' stamp; Anderson Bean has 'AB' on heel counter
Boots: verify the boot has the inner leather stamp identifying ostrich / lizard / caiman / shark / elephant exotic — exotic skins 3-10x cowhide pricing
Hats: leather inner sweatband identifies the maker + 'X' rating (4X, 6X, 10X = beaver-felt blend grade)
Hats: original hatband + dust feather + box adds 20-30%
Snap shirts: pearl snap buttons (genuine MOP vs plastic), embroidered yokes, year-coded label
Buckles: hallmark on the back identifies maker + sterling silver (.925) vs silver-plated overlay
Bolo ties: vintage Native American sterling identifying tribal hallmarks
Spurs: maker's mark stamped on the heel band + silver overlay condition + rowel intact
skip_list: Modern Justin work boot (commodity, not collector tier)
Saddle / tack set (too large/heavy to ship)
Wrangler jeans (covered separately in clothing BOLO)
Fashion-line knockoff (faux western styling without maker mark)

brands.notes: Lucchese is the apex of US cowboy-boot makers — the Classics line + 1883 hand-made line trade $300-1500 used. Exotic skins (ostrich quill, caiman belly, shark, lizard, elephant) command 3-10x premium over standard cowhide. Olathe Boot Co (Kansas, closed 2007) is the post-closure scarcity tier. Custom makers (Stallion, Rocketbuster, Liberty) trade as art objects + workwear ($500-3000). Verify exotic-skin authenticity via the inner leather stamp.

Maker hallmark stamped or sewn into sweatband

brands.notes: Stetson + Resistol are the dominant duo. The 'X' rating drives pricing — 4X is blended wool/fur ($60-130), 10X is pure beaver felt ($130-380), 100X is the apex full-beaver ($400+). American Hat Co (Houston) and Greeley Hat Works are the custom-maker premium tier. Vintage Stetson Open Road from the 1960s-70s has its own LBJ-era cult following. Hats are FRAGILE — ship in original box with crown stuffed.

Rockmount vintage 1960s-70s = founder Jack Weil era (passed 2008 at age 107)
brands.notes: Rockmount Ranch Wear (Denver, founded 1946) + H Bar C (Texas) are the heritage tiers — vintage embroidered chain-stitched western shirts trade $130-400. Pearl-snap buttons (genuine MOP, not plastic) are the immediate quality tell. Scully + Panhandle Slim are mid-tier modern. Smile pockets + sawtooth piping signal vintage Western styling.

brands.notes: Belt buckles are pure $/oz resale gold — palm-sized, ship in a padded envelope, $50-1500+ resale. Edward H Bohlin (Hollywood 1922-80) is the apex — Bohlin pieces are museum-grade collector silver. Sunset Trails / Crumrine / Tom Taylor are the second-tier silversmiths. Hesston-branded annual NFR rodeo trophy buckles (1970s+) are the volume premium tier. Sterling vs silver-plate is HUGE — verify the .925 stamp on the back.

Original tooled-leather cord vs replacement cord
Tip caps original sterling or silver vs base metal replacements
Turquoise grade: Sleeping Beauty (clear blue), Bisbee (matrix), Lone Mountain (apex)
brands.notes: Vintage Native American sterling bolos + concho belts are the resale apex of western jewelry. Tribal hallmarks identify maker (Navajo / Hopi / Zuni). Turquoise grade matters — Sleeping Beauty / Bisbee / Lone Mountain all command premium over generic Chinese-imported turquoise. Bohlin and Sunset Trails are non-Native silversmith premium tier. Concho belts (10-15 conchos on tooled leather) are the $300-1200 set tier — verify each concho is sterling not plated.

brands.notes: Vintage spurs by named makers are the apex collector market in western tack hardware. Edward H Bohlin (Hollywood) — same maker as the buckles — produced spurs for John Wayne and other film stars; pieces trade $1500-8000+. G.S. Garcia (Nevada antique) is museum-tier. Crockett + Buermann are the closed-shop volume premium. Modern hand-engraved makers (Mike Morales, Greg Darnall) trade $400-1800 as art objects. Verify maker's mark on the heel band; sterling-overlay vs nickel-silver-plate matters hugely.

platform_notes.eBay: Dominant marketplace for western wear. Use sold-listings filter — auction-style listings reveal what specific exotic-skin boots / vintage hats / signed buckles actually clear at.
platform_notes.Poshmark: Stronger than eBay for women's western boots (Old Gringo, Lane Boots, Lucchese ladies') + premium hats. Demographic skews younger.
platform_notes.1stDibs: Apex marketplace for Edward H Bohlin pieces + museum-tier antique western. Only worth listing for $500+ pieces.
platform_notes.Heritage Auctions: Antique spurs, bits, and Bohlin silver. Premium consignment fees but reaches the right collector pool for $1K+ pieces.
platform_notes.Cowboys & Indians magazine archives: Reference DB for identifying vintage Stetson / Resistol / Bohlin pieces against catalog photos.
